newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan's Ting Hsin feeds China noodle market.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Ting Hsin feeds China noodle market.

text.p: A new factory built by Taiwan's Ting Hsin International Group in China's Sichuan province is leading the company's assault on the huge southwestern instant noodle market, the China news service said on Monday.

The $60 million plant, which started production in the industrial city of Chongqing in February, could already pump out 760 million packs of the company's "Kang Shifu" brand of noodles a year, the semi-official service said.
The Chinese mainland's most popular instant noodle brand already controlled 60 percent of the market in southwestern China, which includes Sichuan, Yunnan, Guangxi and Guizhou provinces, it said.
The Chongqing factory had six automated instant noodle production lines, bringing to more than 60 the total operated by Ting Hsin in China, it said.
Sales of instant noodles have boomed in China in recent years, boosted by growing spending power among urban residents and increased business travel.
